thesis.description: San Antonio over OKC: spread ladder (1.5/4.5/7.5/10.5/13.5)

prediction_history.rationale: Fading the lower rungs: market mean 25c but SAS+1.5 30c quote is liquidity-limit driven, not probability-driven. OKC favored.
Tightening fade to 18%: order book sat flat across the poll cycle, no surprise late liquidity.
No change — bid stable at 28c, no fresh volume.
No change — bid drifted 28c -> 22c but spread tightened, treating as quote-maker recalibration.

commentary_neighbors.body: Initial framing: spread ladder lets us read the market's implied win-margin distribution; the steeper the no-bid drop across rungs, the more confident the market is in a tight game.

Read the ladder: 30c at SAS+1.5, 22c at +4.5, 13c at +7.5, 12c at +10.5, 9c at +13.5. Curve is internally consistent (monotonic decrease as the spread widens). OKC is the implied favorite. My view: lean slightly below the market mean. Thin liquidity at lower rungs likely over-prices small-margin outcomes because makers cap downside.
Demo API tickers don't have real volume — treat all order-book signal as synthetic. The point of the demo run is exercising the chain pipeline, not extracting alpha.
